b1.texto:
These words are used in class all the time:

- **el libro** (book), **el cuaderno** (notebook), **el ejercicio** (exercise), **la página** (page)
- **el bolígrafo** (pen), **el lápiz** (pencil), **la pizarra** (board)

And these phrases, so you never get stuck:

- **¿En qué página?** (Which page?)
- **Otra vez, por favor.** (Again, please.)
- **No tengo bolígrafo.** (I don't have a pen.)
b2.f0.texto: Open your books to page twenty.
b4.texto:
When the teacher speaks to the whole class, she uses the **vosotros** form:

- **Abrid** el libro. (Open the book.)
- **Cerrad** el cuaderno. (Close the notebook.)
- **Leed** la página veinte. (Read page twenty.)

And when she speaks to just one person:

- **Abre** el libro. (Open the book.)
- **Cierra** el cuaderno. (Close the notebook.)
- **Lee** la página veinte. (Read page twenty.)

Notice: «abrid» is for several people, «abre» for one.
b5.f1.texto: The teacher opens the classroom door.
b5.f2.texto: The students have their books and their notebooks.
b5.f4.texto: Pablo does not have a pen.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía has two and gives him one.
b5.f6.texto: The class starts at nine o’clock.
b5.f7.texto: The teacher explains the homework at the end.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: Pablo says he does not have a pen.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The students already have their books.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The text does not mention chairs.
b7.frase: ___ el libro por la página veinte.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: «abre» is for just one person.
b7.pregunta: Complete the instruction for the whole class.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I don't have a pen».
intro: The things on the desk and the classroom instructions. Today you learn to say what you have and what you are missing.
p.abrir.consejo: It has an irregular participle: «abierto». «He abierto el libro».
p.el bolígrafo.consejo: In Spain people say «bolígrafo» or «boli»; in Mexico you also hear «pluma».
p.el cuaderno.consejo: Careful: it is written with «cu», but it sounds like «kwa».
p.el ejercicio.consejo: You say «el ejercicio dos» or «el ejercicio dos de la página cinco».
p.el libro.consejo: It is written with «b»: «libro». Do not mix it up with «libre», which means free.
p.el lápiz.consejo: The plural is «los lápices»: the «z» changes to «c». The accent goes on «lá».
p.la pizarra.consejo: Double «r»: pi-THA-rra, with a strong rolled r.
p.la página.consejo: The accent goes on «pá». You say «en la página veinte».
p.leer.consejo: The participle is regular: «leído», with an accent because the stressed «í» breaks the pair «eí».
p.los deberes.consejo: It is almost always plural: «los deberes». You can also say «la tarea».
p.otra vez.consejo: A set phrase used to ask for something to be repeated.
p.abrid.consejo: The command for «vosotros», several people: drop the «-r» of «abrir» and add «-d». «Abrid el libro».
p.bolígrafo.consejo: The accent on «í» marks the stress, so it is bo-LI-gra-fo. In Spain people often say «boli».
p.lunes.consejo: Days of the week are not capitalized in Spanish: «lunes», «martes». Singular and plural look the same.
p.cuadernos.consejo: Plural of «cuaderno». The «ua» glides into one syllable: kwa-DER-nos.
p.escuchan.consejo: From «escuchar», to listen on purpose. «Oír» just means to hear a sound. The «ch» is like English «ch».
p.da.consejo: From «dar», to give. «Le da uno» means «gives one to him or her». No accent needed here.
p.leo.consejo: The «yo» form of «leer»: «leo». It has two syllables, LE-o, with the stress on the first.
